items.q: Arc elasticity may be defined as
o: responsiveness measured between two positions using the average of their values as the base
a rectangle whose two corners are the origins of two traders and whose points are possible divisions
the boundary that just touches each short-run average outlay line and shows the least possible outlay per unit as plant size varies
the output at which total receipts are greatest, reached where the extra receipt from one more unit is zero
items.s: Arc elasticity: responsiveness measured between two positions using the average of their values as the base. The other options describe Envelope curve, Edgeworth box, Revenue maximisation.

items.q: The statement “a charge made up of a fixed fee for the right to buy plus a sum for each unit taken” describes which of the following?
o: Natural monopoly
Market power
Price discrimination
Two-part tariff
items.s: Two-part tariff is a charge made up of a fixed fee for the right to buy plus a sum for each unit taken.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Market power?
o: the way output changes when every input is increased by the same proportion
setting a higher charge in the periods when demand presses hardest on limited capacity
the ability of a seller to set a charge above the level that free rivalry would allow
the route traced through the chosen input mixes as a producer grows while input charges stay fixed
items.s: Market power: the ability of a seller to set a charge above the level that free rivalry would allow. The other options describe Returns to scale, Expansion path, Peak-load pricing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Compensating differential.
o: a market dominated by a few large sellers each of whose actions is felt by the others
the habit of repeat buying that makes customers slow to switch to a rival's offer
the extra pay that offsets the unpleasantness or danger of a job
rivalry waged through design, service and promotion instead of through the charge made
items.s: Compensating differential: the extra pay that offsets the unpleasantness or danger of a job. The other options describe Oligopoly, Non-price competition, Brand loyalty.

items.q: Which term is described by “a harm imposed on outsiders that the person causing it does not pay for”?
o: External cost
Adverse selection
Coase theorem
Common resource
items.s: External cost is a harm imposed on outsiders that the person causing it does not pay for.

items.q: Signalling may be defined as
o: an item that, once provided, cannot be withheld from anyone and can be enjoyed by many at once
the relationship giving the least outlay needed to produce each possible amount of output
the use of a costly visible act to show a quality that others cannot easily see
a seller that must accept the ruling charge and can sell any amount at it
items.s: Signalling: the use of a costly visible act to show a quality that others cannot easily see. The other options describe Cost function, Public good, Price taker.

items.q: All of the following belong to Monopoly EXCEPT
o: Natural monopoly
Monopoly
Product differentiation
Market power
items.s: Every other option belongs to Monopoly. “Product differentiation” belongs to Monopolistic competition, not Monopoly.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Two-part tariff?
o: the relationship giving the least outlay needed to produce each possible amount of output
a charge made up of a fixed fee for the right to buy plus a sum for each unit taken
the state in which the worth of the last unit to buyers equals what it took to make
the tendency for worse risks to dominate a market when buyers know more about themselves than sellers do
items.s: Two-part tariff: a charge made up of a fixed fee for the right to buy plus a sum for each unit taken. The other options describe Allocative efficiency, Adverse selection, Cost function.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Price leadership?
o: the practice in which one firm sets the charge and the rest follow it
the state in which every market clears at once and no one wishes to trade further
a natural asset that many may use freely and that one person's use depletes for others
the route traced through the chosen input mixes as a producer grows while input charges stay fixed
items.s: Price leadership: the practice in which one firm sets the charge and the rest follow it. The other options describe Expansion path, Common resource, General equilibrium.

items.q: Backward-bending supply of labour may be defined as
o: a line of supply where one firm can serve the whole market at lower outlay than two or more could
the limit on what a buyer can afford, set by their means and by the charges on the items
a statement of the highest charge buyers will pay for each possible amount of an item
the tendency for extra hours to be offered up to a point and then withdrawn as pay keeps rising
items.s: Backward-bending supply of labour: the tendency for extra hours to be offered up to a point and then withdrawn as pay keeps rising. The other options describe Budget constraint, Inverse demand, Natural monopoly.

items.q: Shut-down point may be defined as
o: the position where receipts no longer cover the outlays that vary with output, so halting loses least
the output at which total receipts just equal total outlay so the surplus is nil
the saving that comes from producing two lines together rather than separately in one firm
the extra receipts a firm gains from employing one more unit of an input
items.s: Shut-down point: the position where receipts no longer cover the outlays that vary with output, so halting loses least. The other options describe Break-even point, Marginal revenue product, Economies of scope.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Oligopoly?
o: the fall in average outlay per unit that comes as a plant or firm grows larger
a line joining all combinations of two items among which a buyer is equally content
the extra risk taking that comes when a person does not bear the cost of the harm they cause
a market dominated by a few large sellers each of whose actions is felt by the others
items.s: Oligopoly: a market dominated by a few large sellers each of whose actions is felt by the others. The other options describe Moral hazard, Economies of scale, Indifference curve.

items.q: The statement “the output at which total receipts just equal total outlay so the surplus is nil” describes which of the following?
o: Consumer surplus
Perfect competition
Break-even point
Allocative efficiency
items.s: Break-even point is the output at which total receipts just equal total outlay so the surplus is nil.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Social welfare function.
o: the state in which every market clears at once and no one wishes to trade further
the saving that comes from producing two lines together rather than separately in one firm
a rule that ranks alternative distributions by the well-being they give to members of society
a model in which rivals match a cut but ignore a rise, so the charge tends to stay put
items.s: Social welfare function: a rule that ranks alternative distributions by the well-being they give to members of society. The other options describe General equilibrium, Kinked demand curve, Economies of scope.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Cartel?
o: the long-run position where the falling demand line just touches the average outlay line so only normal profit is earned
outlay shared by several products that cannot be traced to any one of them
a line joining all combinations of two items among which a buyer is equally content
a formal grouping of independent sellers that acts as one in setting output and charge
items.s: Cartel: a formal grouping of independent sellers that acts as one in setting output and charge. The other options describe Common cost, Indifference curve, Tangency equilibrium.

items.q: Which term is described by “the addition to a firm's outlay from hiring one more unit of an input”?
o: Transfer earnings
Bilateral monopoly
Backward-bending supply of labour
Marginal factor cost
items.s: Marginal factor cost is the addition to a firm's outlay from hiring one more unit of an input.

items.q: Which term is described by “a market dominated by a few large sellers each of whose actions is felt by the others”?
o: Oligopoly
Dominant strategy
Price leadership
Nash equilibrium
items.s: Oligopoly is a market dominated by a few large sellers each of whose actions is felt by the others.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Selling cost?
o: outlay on advertising and promotion aimed at shifting demand rather than at making the item
the practice in which one firm sets the charge and the rest follow it
the state in which every market clears at once and no one wishes to trade further
the quantity of one item that must be given up for one more unit of another while satisfaction stays the same
items.s: Selling cost: outlay on advertising and promotion aimed at shifting demand rather than at making the item. The other options describe General equilibrium, Price leadership, Marginal rate of substitution.

items.q: The statement “a distribution in which no one can be made better off without making another worse off” describes which of the following?
o: Edgeworth box
Pareto efficiency
Contract curve
General equilibrium
items.s: Pareto efficiency is a distribution in which no one can be made better off without making another worse off.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Marginal revenue?
o: the addition to total receipts that comes from one extra unit sold
a line joining all combinations of two inputs that yield the same amount of output
a market with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute and whose entry is blocked
a change that leaves at least one person better off and none worse off
items.s: Marginal revenue: the addition to total receipts that comes from one extra unit sold. The other options describe Isoquant, Pareto improvement, Monopoly.

items.q: The statement “a charge set equal to the harm an activity imposes on outsiders so the seller bears it” describes which of the following?
o: Moral hazard
Coase theorem
Pigouvian tax
Principal-agent problem
items.s: Pigouvian tax is a charge set equal to the harm an activity imposes on outsiders so the seller bears it.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Duopoly?
o: a market dominated by a few large sellers each of whose actions is felt by the others
the quantity of one item that must be given up for one more unit of another while satisfaction stays the same
a market in which exactly two sellers supply the whole of an item
the line relating the amount buyers take to the charge they face when other influences are held fixed
items.s: Duopoly: a market in which exactly two sellers supply the whole of an item. The other options describe Ordinary demand curve, Marginal rate of substitution, Oligopoly.

items.q: The statement “the saving that comes from producing two lines together rather than separately in one firm” describes which of the following?
o: Envelope curve
Long-run average cost
Economies of scope
Avoidable cost
items.s: Economies of scope is the saving that comes from producing two lines together rather than separately in one firm.

items.q: The statement “the change in purchases that follows solely from a change in purchasing power when relative charges stay fixed” describes which of the following?
o: Budget constraint
Giffen good
Income effect
Indifference curve
items.s: Income effect is the change in purchases that follows solely from a change in purchasing power when relative charges stay fixed.

items.q: The statement “an arrangement among rivals to fix charges or share markets instead of competing” describes which of the following?
o: Kinked demand curve
Duopoly
Dominant strategy
Collusion
items.s: Collusion is an arrangement among rivals to fix charges or share markets instead of competing.

items.q: The statement “outlay on advertising and promotion aimed at shifting demand rather than at making the item” describes which of the following?
o: Brand loyalty
Non-price competition
Selling cost
Monopolistic competition
items.s: Selling cost is outlay on advertising and promotion aimed at shifting demand rather than at making the item.

items.q: Which term is described by “the extra receipts a firm gains from employing one more unit of an input”?
o: Compensating differential
Marginal revenue product
Economic rent
Marginal factor cost
items.s: Marginal revenue product is the extra receipts a firm gains from employing one more unit of an input.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Isocost line?
o: a straight boundary marking every mix of inputs that requires the same total outlay
the rise in average outlay per unit that sets in when a firm becomes too large to manage well
an arrangement among rivals to fix charges or share markets instead of competing
a market of many sellers whose items are close but not identical substitutes
items.s: Isocost line: a straight boundary marking every mix of inputs that requires the same total outlay. The other options describe Collusion, Monopolistic competition, Diseconomies of scale.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Cost function.
o: the relationship giving the least outlay needed to produce each possible amount of output
the relationship between a household's total outlay and the quantity of one item it buys
the use of a costly visible act to show a quality that others cannot easily see
the smallest size at which average outlay per unit has fallen as far as it will go
items.s: Cost function: the relationship giving the least outlay needed to produce each possible amount of output. The other options describe Engel curve, Minimum efficient scale, Signalling.

items.q: Which term is described by “the saving that comes from producing two lines together rather than separately in one firm”?
o: Economies of scope
Common cost
Avoidable cost
Sunk cost
items.s: Economies of scope is the saving that comes from producing two lines together rather than separately in one firm.

items.q: The statement “the decline in the work needed per unit as cumulative output rises with experience” describes which of the following?
o: Learning curve
Economies of scale
Minimum efficient scale
Diseconomies of scale
items.s: Learning curve is the decline in the work needed per unit as cumulative output rises with experience.

items.q: Which term is described by “the decline in the work needed per unit as cumulative output rises with experience”?
o: Expansion path
Learning curve
Diseconomies of scale
Returns to scale
items.s: Learning curve is the decline in the work needed per unit as cumulative output rises with experience.

items.q: Perfect competition may be defined as
o: a market in which many small sellers offer an identical item and none of them can affect its charge
the output at which total receipts just equal total outlay so the surplus is nil
a market in which exactly two sellers supply the whole of an item
the rise in average outlay per unit that sets in when a firm becomes too large to manage well
items.s: Perfect competition: a market in which many small sellers offer an identical item and none of them can affect its charge. The other options describe Diseconomies of scale, Break-even point, Duopoly.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Duopoly?
o: a market in which exactly two sellers supply the whole of an item
the extra pay that offsets the unpleasantness or danger of a job
the fall in average outlay per unit that comes as a plant or firm grows larger
a line joining all combinations of two items among which a buyer is equally content
items.s: Duopoly: a market in which exactly two sellers supply the whole of an item. The other options describe Compensating differential, Indifference curve, Economies of scale.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Compensating differential?
o: the extra risk taking that comes when a person does not bear the cost of the harm they cause
the extra pay that offsets the unpleasantness or danger of a job
the addition to total receipts that comes from one extra unit sold
the change in purchases that follows solely from a change in purchasing power when relative charges stay fixed
items.s: Compensating differential: the extra pay that offsets the unpleasantness or danger of a job. The other options describe Marginal revenue, Moral hazard, Income effect.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Contract curve?
o: outlay already made that cannot be recovered whatever is decided now
the extra risk taking that comes when a person does not bear the cost of the harm they cause
the ranking a buyer gives to all the bundles of items open to them, from most to least wanted
the set of efficient divisions from which no further mutually gainful trade exists
items.s: Contract curve: the set of efficient divisions from which no further mutually gainful trade exists. The other options describe Preference ordering, Moral hazard, Sunk cost.

items.q: Non-price competition may be defined as
o: a setting where each side's rational self-interest leaves both worse off than cooperation would
a course of action that gives the best result whatever the other player does
a set of choices where no player can gain by changing their own alone
rivalry waged through design, service and promotion instead of through the charge made
items.s: Non-price competition: rivalry waged through design, service and promotion instead of through the charge made. The other options describe Prisoner's dilemma, Nash equilibrium, Dominant strategy.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Long-run average cost?
o: a formal grouping of independent sellers that acts as one in setting output and charge
the least outlay per unit attainable when every input can be varied and the best plant size is chosen
a change that leaves at least one person better off and none worse off
the limit on what a buyer can afford, set by their means and by the charges on the items
items.s: Long-run average cost: the least outlay per unit attainable when every input can be varied and the best plant size is chosen. The other options describe Cartel, Pareto improvement, Budget constraint.

items.q: Price taker may be defined as
o: a seller that must accept the ruling charge and can sell any amount at it
the fall in combined buyer and seller benefit when output is held below the point where worth and outlay are equal
rivalry waged through design, service and promotion instead of through the charge made
a market in which many small sellers offer an identical item and none of them can affect its charge
items.s: Price taker: a seller that must accept the ruling charge and can sell any amount at it. The other options describe Non-price competition, Deadweight loss, Perfect competition.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Consumer surplus?
o: the change in purchases that follows solely from a change in purchasing power when relative charges stay fixed
the excess of what buyers would have been willing to pay over what they actually pay
a market with a single buyer of an input or of a product
a rule that ranks alternative distributions by the well-being they give to members of society
items.s: Consumer surplus: the excess of what buyers would have been willing to pay over what they actually pay. The other options describe Social welfare function, Income effect, Monopsony.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Selling cost?
o: outlay on advertising and promotion aimed at shifting demand rather than at making the item
a market in which exactly two sellers supply the whole of an item
the ranking a buyer gives to all the bundles of items open to them, from most to least wanted
the least outlay per unit attainable when every input can be varied and the best plant size is chosen
items.s: Selling cost: outlay on advertising and promotion aimed at shifting demand rather than at making the item. The other options describe Preference ordering, Duopoly, Long-run average cost.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Monopolistic competition.
o: the position where receipts no longer cover the outlays that vary with output, so halting loses least
the relationship between a household's total outlay and the quantity of one item it buys
a market of many sellers whose items are close but not identical substitutes
the state in which the worth of the last unit to buyers equals what it took to make
items.s: Monopolistic competition: a market of many sellers whose items are close but not identical substitutes. The other options describe Engel curve, Shut-down point, Allocative efficiency.

items.q: Which term is described by “the smallest size at which average outlay per unit has fallen as far as it will go”?
o: Isocost line
Minimum efficient scale
Learning curve
Economies of scale
items.s: Minimum efficient scale is the smallest size at which average outlay per unit has fallen as far as it will go.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Average revenue?
o: an item whose sales rise when its charge rises because it takes a large share of a poor buyer's outlay
total receipts divided by the number of units sold, equal to the charge per unit when all pay the same
a formal grouping of independent sellers that acts as one in setting output and charge
the ranking a buyer gives to all the bundles of items open to them, from most to least wanted
items.s: Average revenue: total receipts divided by the number of units sold, equal to the charge per unit when all pay the same. The other options describe Cartel, Preference ordering, Giffen good.

items.q: All of the following belong to Consumer preferences and choice EXCEPT
o: Isocost line
Preference ordering
Indifference curve
Marginal rate of substitution
items.s: Every other option belongs to Consumer preferences and choice. “Isocost line” belongs to Production in the long run, not Consumer preferences and choice.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Market power?
o: the practice in which one firm sets the charge and the rest follow it
a set of choices where no player can gain by changing their own alone
the limit on what a buyer can afford, set by their means and by the charges on the items
the ability of a seller to set a charge above the level that free rivalry would allow
items.s: Market power: the ability of a seller to set a charge above the level that free rivalry would allow. The other options describe Price leadership, Budget constraint, Nash equilibrium.

items.q: Which term is described by “a market of many sellers whose items are close but not identical substitutes”?
o: Excess capacity
Monopolistic competition
Non-price competition
Tangency equilibrium
items.s: Monopolistic competition is a market of many sellers whose items are close but not identical substitutes.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Price taker.
o: the excess of what sellers receive over the least they would have accepted
outlay that would not be incurred if a particular activity were dropped
a change that leaves at least one person better off and none worse off
a seller that must accept the ruling charge and can sell any amount at it
items.s: Price taker: a seller that must accept the ruling charge and can sell any amount at it. The other options describe Producer surplus, Pareto improvement, Avoidable cost.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Monopoly?
o: a charge set equal to the harm an activity imposes on outsiders so the seller bears it
the excess of what sellers receive over the least they would have accepted
a market with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute and whose entry is blocked
outlay already made that cannot be recovered whatever is decided now
items.s: Monopoly: a market with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute and whose entry is blocked. The other options describe Producer surplus, Sunk cost, Pigouvian tax.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Pigouvian tax?
o: a rule that ranks alternative distributions by the well-being they give to members of society
the claim that clear ownership rights let parties bargain to an efficient result when dealing is costless
a market with one seller facing one buyer, so the outcome rests on bargaining
a charge set equal to the harm an activity imposes on outsiders so the seller bears it
items.s: Pigouvian tax: a charge set equal to the harm an activity imposes on outsiders so the seller bears it. The other options describe Bilateral monopoly, Coase theorem, Social welfare function.

items.q: All of the following belong to Oligopoly and strategic behaviour EXCEPT
o: Collusion
Oligopoly
Duopoly
Common resource
items.s: Every other option belongs to Oligopoly and strategic behaviour. “Common resource” belongs to Market failure and information, not Oligopoly and strategic behaviour.

o: Excess capacity
Product differentiation
Market power
Monopolistic competition
items.s: Every other option belongs to Monopolistic competition. “Market power” belongs to Monopoly, not Monopolistic competition.

items.q: Which term is described by “the quantity of one item that must be given up for one more unit of another while satisfaction stays the same”?
o: Giffen good
Indifference curve
Marginal rate of substitution
Engel curve
items.s: Marginal rate of substitution is the quantity of one item that must be given up for one more unit of another while satisfaction stays the same.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Rent seeking?
o: the least outlay per unit attainable when every input can be varied and the best plant size is chosen
spending resources to win or keep a privileged position rather than to produce anything
a change that leaves at least one person better off and none worse off
an item whose sales rise when its charge rises because it takes a large share of a poor buyer's outlay
items.s: Rent seeking: spending resources to win or keep a privileged position rather than to produce anything. The other options describe Long-run average cost, Pareto improvement, Giffen good.

items.q: Giffen good may be defined as
o: the features, brand, packaging or site that make buyers treat similar offers as distinct
an item whose sales rise when its charge rises because it takes a large share of a poor buyer's outlay
an arrangement among rivals to fix charges or share markets instead of competing
a rectangle whose two corners are the origins of two traders and whose points are possible divisions
items.s: Giffen good: an item whose sales rise when its charge rises because it takes a large share of a poor buyer's outlay. The other options describe Edgeworth box, Collusion, Product differentiation.

items.q: All of the following belong to General equilibrium and welfare EXCEPT
o: General equilibrium
Coase theorem
Pareto improvement
Pareto efficiency
items.s: Every other option belongs to General equilibrium and welfare. “Coase theorem” belongs to Market failure and information, not General equilibrium and welfare.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Pigouvian tax.
o: a charge set equal to the harm an activity imposes on outsiders so the seller bears it
the route traced through the chosen input mixes as a producer grows while input charges stay fixed
charging different buyers different amounts for the same item where the gap is not explained by outlay
the change in purchases that follows solely from a change in purchasing power when relative charges stay fixed
items.s: Pigouvian tax: a charge set equal to the harm an activity imposes on outsiders so the seller bears it. The other options describe Expansion path, Price discrimination, Income effect.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Isocost line.
o: the excess of what sellers receive over the least they would have accepted
a market dominated by a few large sellers each of whose actions is felt by the others
a straight boundary marking every mix of inputs that requires the same total outlay
a distribution in which no one can be made better off without making another worse off
items.s: Isocost line: a straight boundary marking every mix of inputs that requires the same total outlay. The other options describe Pareto efficiency, Producer surplus, Oligopoly.

a line joining all combinations of two inputs that yield the same amount of output
the boundary that just touches each short-run average outlay line and shows the least possible outlay per unit as plant size varies
the fall in combined buyer and seller benefit when output is held below the point where worth and outlay are equal
items.s: Deadweight loss: the fall in combined buyer and seller benefit when output is held below the point where worth and outlay are equal. The other options describe X-inefficiency, Isoquant, Envelope curve.

items.q: Which term is described by “the state in which the worth of the last unit to buyers equals what it took to make”?

Shut-down point
Allocative efficiency
Producer surplus

the state in which the worth of the last unit to buyers equals what it took to make
the way output changes when every input is increased by the same proportion
the state in which every market clears at once and no one wishes to trade further
items.s: General equilibrium: the state in which every market clears at once and no one wishes to trade further. The other options describe Peak-load pricing, Allocative efficiency, Returns to scale.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Consumer surplus.
o: the boundary that just touches each short-run average outlay line and shows the least possible outlay per unit as plant size varies
the excess of what buyers would have been willing to pay over what they actually pay
rivalry waged through design, service and promotion instead of through the charge made
a model in which rivals match a cut but ignore a rise, so the charge tends to stay put
items.s: Consumer surplus: the excess of what buyers would have been willing to pay over what they actually pay. The other options describe Kinked demand curve, Envelope curve, Non-price competition.

items.q: Which term is described by “the boundary that just touches each short-run average outlay line and shows the least possible outlay per unit as plant size varies”?
o: Long-run average cost
Sunk cost
Cost function
Envelope curve
items.s: Envelope curve is the boundary that just touches each short-run average outlay line and shows the least possible outlay per unit as plant size varies.

items.q: The statement “the habit of repeat buying that makes customers slow to switch to a rival's offer” describes which of the following?
o: Tangency equilibrium
Non-price competition
Selling cost
Brand loyalty
items.s: Brand loyalty is the habit of repeat buying that makes customers slow to switch to a rival's offer.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines X-inefficiency?
o: the slack that appears when a protected firm stops pressing its outlay down to the least possible
the gap between the output that would minimise average outlay and the smaller amount actually sold in the long run
the fall in average outlay per unit that comes as a plant or firm grows larger
an arrangement among rivals to fix charges or share markets instead of competing
items.s: X-inefficiency: the slack that appears when a protected firm stops pressing its outlay down to the least possible. The other options describe Excess capacity, Collusion, Economies of scale.

items.q: Which term is described by “the route traced through the chosen input mixes as a producer grows while input charges stay fixed”?
o: Diseconomies of scale
Expansion path
Learning curve
Minimum efficient scale
items.s: Expansion path is the route traced through the chosen input mixes as a producer grows while input charges stay fixed.

items.q: Which term is described by “the excess of what sellers receive over the least they would have accepted”?
o: Price taker
Shut-down point
Producer surplus
Consumer surplus
items.s: Producer surplus is the excess of what sellers receive over the least they would have accepted.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Economies of scale?
o: the habit of repeat buying that makes customers slow to switch to a rival's offer
the fall in combined buyer and seller benefit when output is held below the point where worth and outlay are equal
the fall in average outlay per unit that comes as a plant or firm grows larger
a seller that must accept the ruling charge and can sell any amount at it
items.s: Economies of scale: the fall in average outlay per unit that comes as a plant or firm grows larger. The other options describe Deadweight loss, Brand loyalty, Price taker.

items.q: Which term is described by “a market with one seller facing one buyer, so the outcome rests on bargaining”?
o: Economic rent
Bilateral monopoly
Marginal factor cost
Compensating differential
items.s: Bilateral monopoly is a market with one seller facing one buyer, so the outcome rests on bargaining.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Non-price competition?
o: the least outlay per unit attainable when every input can be varied and the best plant size is chosen
the fall in combined buyer and seller benefit when output is held below the point where worth and outlay are equal
rivalry waged through design, service and promotion instead of through the charge made
a setting where each side's rational self-interest leaves both worse off than cooperation would
items.s: Non-price competition: rivalry waged through design, service and promotion instead of through the charge made. The other options describe Deadweight loss, Prisoner's dilemma, Long-run average cost.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Revealed preference?
o: the practice in which one firm sets the charge and the rest follow it
the features, brand, packaging or site that make buyers treat similar offers as distinct
the inference that a buyer likes one bundle better than another because they chose it when both were affordable
the ratio of a small proportional change in amount to a small proportional change in charge at one position
items.s: Revealed preference: the inference that a buyer likes one bundle better than another because they chose it when both were affordable. The other options describe Point elasticity, Price leadership, Product differentiation.

items.q: Marginal rate of substitution may be defined as
o: the fall in combined buyer and seller benefit when output is held below the point where worth and outlay are equal
an arrangement among rivals to fix charges or share markets instead of competing

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Arc elasticity.
o: responsiveness measured between two positions using the average of their values as the base
total receipts divided by the number of units sold, equal to the charge per unit when all pay the same
the line relating the amount buyers take to the charge they face when other influences are held fixed
a statement of the highest charge buyers will pay for each possible amount of an item
items.s: Arc elasticity: responsiveness measured between two positions using the average of their values as the base. The other options describe Inverse demand, Average revenue, Ordinary demand curve.

items.q: The correct meaning of Two-part tariff is
o: a charge made up of a fixed fee for the right to buy plus a sum for each unit taken
spending resources to win or keep a privileged position rather than to produce anything
setting a higher charge in the periods when demand presses hardest on limited capacity
a line of supply where one firm can serve the whole market at lower outlay than two or more could
items.s: Two-part tariff: a charge made up of a fixed fee for the right to buy plus a sum for each unit taken. The other options describe Natural monopoly, Rent seeking, Peak-load pricing.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Engel curve.
o: a line joining all combinations of two items among which a buyer is equally content
the inference that a buyer likes one bundle better than another because they chose it when both were affordable
the relationship between a household's total outlay and the quantity of one item it buys
the quantity of one item that must be given up for one more unit of another while satisfaction stays the same
items.s: Engel curve: the relationship between a household's total outlay and the quantity of one item it buys. The other options describe Revealed preference, Indifference curve, Marginal rate of substitution.

items.q: “the state in which every market clears at once and no one wishes to trade further” is the definition of
o: Edgeworth box
General equilibrium
Contract curve
Pareto efficiency
items.s: General equilibrium is the state in which every market clears at once and no one wishes to trade further.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the inference that a buyer likes one bundle better than another because they chose it when both were affordable”
o: Indifference curve
Giffen good
Income effect
Revealed preference
items.s: Revealed preference is the inference that a buyer likes one bundle better than another because they chose it when both were affordable.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a market in which exactly two sellers supply the whole of an item”
o: Nash equilibrium
Prisoner's dilemma
Price leadership
Duopoly
items.s: Duopoly is a market in which exactly two sellers supply the whole of an item.

items.q: In this course, Allocative efficiency refers to
o: the excess of what sellers receive over the least they would have accepted
a market in which many small sellers offer an identical item and none of them can affect its charge
the state in which the worth of the last unit to buyers equals what it took to make
a seller that must accept the ruling charge and can sell any amount at it
items.s: Allocative efficiency: the state in which the worth of the last unit to buyers equals what it took to make. The other options describe Price taker, Producer surplus, Perfect competition.

items.q: The correct meaning of Giffen good is
o: the relationship between a household's total outlay and the quantity of one item it buys
the limit on what a buyer can afford, set by their means and by the charges on the items
an item whose sales rise when its charge rises because it takes a large share of a poor buyer's outlay
the quantity of one item that must be given up for one more unit of another while satisfaction stays the same
items.s: Giffen good: an item whose sales rise when its charge rises because it takes a large share of a poor buyer's outlay. The other options describe Budget constraint, Marginal rate of substitution, Engel curve.

items.q: In this course, Economic rent refers to
o: the tendency for extra hours to be offered up to a point and then withdrawn as pay keeps rising
the part of a payment above the least needed to keep a factor in its present use
the extra receipts a firm gains from employing one more unit of an input
a market with a single buyer of an input or of a product
items.s: Economic rent: the part of a payment above the least needed to keep a factor in its present use. The other options describe Monopsony, Marginal revenue product, Backward-bending supply of labour.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “outlay that would not be incurred if a particular activity were dropped”
o: Avoidable cost
Long-run average cost
Cost function
Common cost
items.s: Avoidable cost is outlay that would not be incurred if a particular activity were dropped.

items.q: “the rise in average outlay per unit that sets in when a firm becomes too large to manage well” is the definition of
o: Learning curve
Expansion path
Diseconomies of scale
Isoquant
items.s: Diseconomies of scale is the rise in average outlay per unit that sets in when a firm becomes too large to manage well.

items.q: “the tendency for worse risks to dominate a market when buyers know more about themselves than sellers do” is the definition of
o: Coase theorem
Public good
Adverse selection
Common resource
items.s: Adverse selection is the tendency for worse risks to dominate a market when buyers know more about themselves than sellers do.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Income effect?
o: a line joining all combinations of two items among which a buyer is equally content
the limit on what a buyer can afford, set by their means and by the charges on the items
the change in purchases that follows solely from a change in purchasing power when relative charges stay fixed
the quantity of one item that must be given up for one more unit of another while satisfaction stays the same
items.s: Income effect: the change in purchases that follows solely from a change in purchasing power when relative charges stay fixed. The other options describe Budget constraint, Indifference curve, Marginal rate of substitution.

items.q: In this course, Price discrimination refers to
o: charging different buyers different amounts for the same item where the gap is not explained by outlay
a market with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute and whose entry is blocked
spending resources to win or keep a privileged position rather than to produce anything
a line of supply where one firm can serve the whole market at lower outlay than two or more could
items.s: Price discrimination: charging different buyers different amounts for the same item where the gap is not explained by outlay. The other options describe Natural monopoly, Rent seeking, Monopoly.

items.q: The correct meaning of Moral hazard is
o: the use of a costly visible act to show a quality that others cannot easily see
the extra risk taking that comes when a person does not bear the cost of the harm they cause
the claim that clear ownership rights let parties bargain to an efficient result when dealing is costless
an item that, once provided, cannot be withheld from anyone and can be enjoyed by many at once
items.s: Moral hazard: the extra risk taking that comes when a person does not bear the cost of the harm they cause. The other options describe Signalling, Public good, Coase theorem.

items.q: “a distribution in which no one can be made better off without making another worse off” is the definition of
o: Pareto efficiency
Pareto improvement
Social welfare function
General equilibrium
items.s: Pareto efficiency is a distribution in which no one can be made better off without making another worse off.

items.q: Oligopoly may be defined as
o: a market dominated by a few large sellers each of whose actions is felt by the others
an arrangement among rivals to fix charges or share markets instead of competing
a model in which rivals match a cut but ignore a rise, so the charge tends to stay put
a setting where each side's rational self-interest leaves both worse off than cooperation would
items.s: Oligopoly: a market dominated by a few large sellers each of whose actions is felt by the others. The other options describe Collusion, Prisoner's dilemma, Kinked demand curve.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Long-run average cost?
o: outlay that would not be incurred if a particular activity were dropped
the boundary that just touches each short-run average outlay line and shows the least possible outlay per unit as plant size varies
outlay already made that cannot be recovered whatever is decided now
the least outlay per unit attainable when every input can be varied and the best plant size is chosen
items.s: Long-run average cost: the least outlay per unit attainable when every input can be varied and the best plant size is chosen. The other options describe Avoidable cost, Sunk cost, Envelope curve.

items.q: The correct meaning of Principal-agent problem is
o: an item that, once provided, cannot be withheld from anyone and can be enjoyed by many at once
a charge set equal to the harm an activity imposes on outsiders so the seller bears it
the extra risk taking that comes when a person does not bear the cost of the harm they cause
the difficulty that arises when a person acting for another has aims that differ from that other's
items.s: Principal-agent problem: the difficulty that arises when a person acting for another has aims that differ from that other's. The other options describe Moral hazard, Public good, Pigouvian tax.

items.q: “a charge made up of a fixed fee for the right to buy plus a sum for each unit taken” is the definition of
o: Two-part tariff
X-inefficiency
Price discrimination
Rent seeking
items.s: Two-part tariff is a charge made up of a fixed fee for the right to buy plus a sum for each unit taken.

items.q: In this course, Market power refers to
o: the ability of a seller to set a charge above the level that free rivalry would allow
charging different buyers different amounts for the same item where the gap is not explained by outlay
a market with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute and whose entry is blocked
the slack that appears when a protected firm stops pressing its outlay down to the least possible
items.s: Market power: the ability of a seller to set a charge above the level that free rivalry would allow. The other options describe Monopoly, Price discrimination, X-inefficiency.
